title: fix(plugin-grid): a server-grouped grid selects field names, never column objects (objectui#11105)
body:
Fixes #11105

## What was wrong

A grid list view that declares `grouping` and writes its `columns` as objects (`{ field, width, ... }`) showed `Unknown field '[object Object]'` (400 INVALID_FIELD) in every group on `@objectstack` 17.5.0, instead of the group's rows.

Mechanism, re-read on `origin/main` before the change:

- `ListView`'s grid branch hands its effective column entries to the grid under both keys: `baseProps` carry `fields: effectiveFields`, and the grid case adds `columns: effectiveFields`.
- In `ObjectGrid`'s load effect, `getSelectFields()` read the `schemaColumns` branch through `columnIdentity`, but the `schemaFields` branch (checked first) returned its entries unmapped: `return withHarvestedFields(ensureId((schemaFields as any[]).filter(passesProjectionGate)));`. The column objects went into `$select`.
- `@object-ui/data-objectstack` serializes `$select` with `selectFields.join(',')`, which prints `[object Object]`.
- Server-side grid grouping (objectui#7189) builds this query once (`setGroupRowQuery(groupQuery)`) and `useServerGroupRows` sends it on every group's row page. The 17.5 server refuses unknown select keys, so the latent projection bug became an error in every group. Before server grouping, a grouped grid under `ListView` received inline rows, so this projection never reached the wire.

## The change

Inside `getSelectFields()` only: both branches now run one projection, `projectFieldNames`: gate each entry (`passesProjectionGate`), read its field name through `columnIdentity`, drop entries with no identity. `$select` carries names only (plus `id`, the grouping fields and the predicate operands, as before). A `fields` entry that is already a name comes back unchanged, so string projections ask for exactly what they asked for before.

The diff stays inside `getSelectFields()`. Draft PR #10278 also edits `ObjectGrid.tsx`'s fetch effect (the `params` window and the effect's dependency list); the two change different lines.

## Tests

New pin: `packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/serverGroupedSelectIdentity-11105.test.tsx`, describe `a server-grouped grid with object columns asks for field names (objectui#11105)`. It mounts `ObjectGrid` with the node `ListView` builds (the same object entries under `fields` and `columns`) over a data source that answers the group header query and, like the 17.5 server, refuses a `$select` entry that is not a declared field name.

- `every group page selects names only — id, the columns, and the grouping key`: both group row pages send `['id', 'name', 'list_price', 'category']`, every group shows its rows, and no `group-rows-error-*` element renders.
- `an entry with no field identity is left out of the projection, not sent`: a `{ width: 80 }` entry is dropped.
- `the ungrouped fetch the grid makes for itself selects names too`: the flat fetch uses the same projection.
- `CONTROL — the same grid with string columns selects the same names`: green before and after the fix.

Reverse verification, with the fix committed first (`a014b30b`): `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (from the objectstack checkout) swapped the new `schemaFields` return line back to the BASE line (anchor hit x1 to x0, blob changed on disk) and ran the file:

```
× every group page selects names only — id, the columns, and the grouping key
× an entry with no field identity is left out of the projection, not sent
× the ungrouped fetch the grid makes for itself selects names too
AssertionError: expected [ 'id', …(3) ] to deeply equal [ 'id', 'name', 'list_price', …(1) ]
Tests  3 failed | 1 passed (4)
```

The CONTROL stayed green. The restore was proven (blob after restore equals the HEAD blob, and `git diff HEAD` is empty). The subject is imported from `../ObjectGrid` source, so no `dist` build sits between the mutation and the run.

## Gates (at head `3541d68b`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-grid/`: 168 files, 1557 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-grid type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0, after building the dependency closure (`turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/plugin-grid^...`, 13 tasks). `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` includes the new test file.
- ESLint on the two touched source files: 0 errors. The new test has 0 warnings. `ObjectGrid.tsx` has 207 warnings, down from 209 on BASE, because two `any` casts left. Type-aware linting is not configured, so the diff cannot change a verdict in an untouched file.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `pnpm changeset:check`, `pnpm check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `pnpm check:control-bytes`, `pnpm check:phantom-deps`, `pnpm check:test-path-roots`, `pnpm check:unreferenced-sources`, `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals`: all exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on the three changed paths: NOT GOVERNED.
- `pnpm check:changeset-claims` lists five pending changesets that name `ObjectGrid.tsx`. I read each paragraph. None of them describes the `$select` projection, so none is made false by this change.

Changeset: `.changeset/11105-grouped-grid-selects-field-names.md`, `@object-ui/plugin-grid: patch`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Adapter hardening was not done here.** The issue also suggests that `@object-ui/data-objectstack` refuse a non-string `$select` entry instead of joining it. I left it out of this PR because neither option is small and clearly safe. Skipping the entry silently would be a lenient fallback of the kind AGENTS.md #0.1 rules out: it hides the producer's bug. Refusing it adds a new client-side error surface at two serialization sites (`rawFindWithPopulate` and `convertQueryParams`). It would also change behaviour for any other caller that sends a non-name entry to a server that ignores unknown select keys. That needs its own decision on the error's code and wording.
- **Where the object entries come from.** `ObjectGridSchema.fields` is declared `string[]` in both the TypeScript interface and the zod mirror (`fields: z.array(z.string()).optional()`). `ListView` passes the column objects under that key anyway, because `baseProps` share `fields` across every child view. This fix reads names on the consumer side, which is the route the dispatch chose. The other option is to stop `ListView`'s grid node from carrying the objects under `fields`, which is on the producer side. That touches every child view's handoff and is outside this change. After this fix, no grid reader of `schema.fields` gives a wrong answer for that node. The render and expand paths prefer `columns`. No carrier.
